data.title: Rollback
data.tagline: Rollback restores a system or configuration to a previous known-good state to stop current impact.
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish rollback from a forward fix and require both version and health signals as rollback evidence.
data.description: If v2 causes abnormal login errors, switch the running image or configuration back to v1 and check the live version, login result, and error rate recover. It aims to reduce impact first. Fixing the issue and shipping a new version later is a forward fix, not rollback.

learning.assumes: You know a release can create a problem that needs immediate impact reduction.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish rollback from a forward fix and require both version and health signals as rollback evidence.

distinctions.label: Feature flag
distinctions.explanation: Rollback restores a system or configuration to a previously known-good state. A Feature Flag can disable one code path without necessarily changing the deployed version.

explanation.title: Restore a known-good state to reduce impact
explanation.text: When a new version materially affects people, returning to a verified version or configuration can stop spread quickly. State the target clearly rather than saying only “restore it.”

explanation.title: A completed switch is not recovered health
explanation.text: First confirm the target version is actually running, then inspect login success, error rate, or key action recovery. If metrics do not recover, the problem may extend beyond this version.

data.boundary: Rollback is not fixing code and shipping another version; that is a forward fix. It also differs from disabling a feature flag: a flag stops one new path, while rollback restores a whole version or configuration to a prior state.

lessonPractice.title: After v2 raises login error rate, the team switches the image back to v1. What completes rollback verification?

options.label: Confirm production is actually running v1 and that login error rate and login success recover
options.feedback: Correct. Prove both that the target is running and that the user-impact signal recovered.

options.label: End when the command reports success, without checking production metrics
options.feedback: A successful command does not guarantee traffic uses the target version or the anomaly disappeared.

options.label: Immediately start fixing v2 and ignore the current live state
options.feedback: A forward fix can follow, but first prove the present impact has stopped.

data.agentPrompt: If login error rate crosses its threshold, roll production back from v2 to the last known-good v1. Afterward, confirm both that v1 is actually running and that login error and success rates recovered; report both pieces of evidence.
